reason: No proposal has measured evidence of a gain, and the historical scores are noisy. Rank low-risk loop changes first: pointer updates, explicit K blocks, and full-tile handling preserve the layout, FP32 MOPA work, and accumulation order. Then test K unrolling and input reuse, which may help scheduling but can raise register pressure or change tile efficiency. Region fusion and layout or packing changes alter more of the timed path and have uncertain tradeoffs. The B-transpose scalar loop gives up SME MOPA, so it ranks last. These are test priorities, not claims about a cache bottleneck or expected speedups.
